chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from a man, from Yahya ibn Ubada, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A wet twig of the length of a cubit is taken and placed, and he gestured with his hand from his collarbone to his hand, [saying it is] wrapped with his garment.
He said, And the man said, I met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) afterwards and asked him about it, so he said: Yes, I had narrated it to Yahya ibn Ubada.

key_terms.جَرِيدَةٌ: A fresh palm branch or twig

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual significance of placing a wet twig on the deceased's chest in Shia burial practices?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the specific Sunnah of placing a fresh palm twig (*jarid*) on the chest of the deceased during shrouding, a practice rooted in the teachings of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). The verification by Yahya ibn Ubada underscores the reliability of this transmission within Shia jurisprudence, linking the physical act to spiritual symbolism. The use of a 'wet' twig likely signifies freshness and vitality, serving as a tangible reminder of resurrection and the continuity of life beyond death.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from a man, from Yahya Bin Ubada, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

You should take a wet twig of the measurement of a cubit and you should place it’, and he<sup>asws</sup> gestured by his<sup>asws</sup> from his<sup>asws</sup> clavicle up to his<sup>asws</sup> hand’, ‘wrapped with his cloth (shroud)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And the man who met Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said afterwards, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about it, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, I<sup>asws</sup> had narrated with it to Yahya Bin Ubada (the narrator of this Hadeeth)’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from a man from Yahya ibn ‘Ubadah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Two pieces of fresh twigs one yard in length are placed with a deceased’ - pointing with his hand - ‘one end from collar bones to the hands wrapped with cloth.’

He (the narrator) has said that the man then said, ‘I met abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, afterwards and asked him (the Imam) about it. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes I spoke about it to Yahya ibn ‘Ubadah.’”
